sec: Hyperbilirubinemia & transaminases · classification, kinetics and ALT vs AST

items.q: Which cutoff percentages define indirect versus direct forms of elevated bilirubin?
items.exp: Indirect hyperbilirubinemia is defined as indirect bilirubin >= 85% of total bilirubin, whereas direct hyperbilirubinemia is direct bilirubin >= 50% of total bilirubin. (Book p988)

items.q: What proportion of the pigment pool is direct in mixed hyperbilirubinemia (hepatic jaundice)?
items.exp: Mixed hyperbilirubinemia / hepatic jaundice is defined by direct bilirubin comprising 15–50% of total bilirubin. (Book p988)

items.q: Match each inherited unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia with its residual UDP-glucuronosyltransferase activity — 1) Gilbert syndrome 2) Crigler-Najjar syndrome type II … A) <10% enzyme activity B) Approximately 30% enzyme activity
items.exp: Gilbert syndrome features partial deficiency with ~30% enzyme activity, whereas Crigler-Najjar syndrome type II features severe deficiency with <10% activity. (Book p988)

items.q: What is the most common overall cause of unconjugated (indirect) hyperbilirubinemia?
items.exp: The page annotates extravascular hemolysis with '(m/c)' under the indirect hyperbilirubinemia branch. (Book p988)

items.q: Which of the following drugs is NOT listed as a cause of unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia on this page?
opts: Steroids taken in excess to decrease bilirubin
items.exp: Rifampicin and probenecid cause indirect hyperbilirubinemia, and excess steroids are noted in the margin; chlorpromazine causes cholestatic hepatitis (discussed on p991). (Book p988)

items.q: What are the normal serum Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT) levels for males and females, and what is the overall average upper limit?
opts: Male < 23 U/L, Female < 19 U/L, Average < 30 U/L
Male < 45 U/L, Female < 35 U/L, Average < 50 U/L
Male < 15 U/L, Female < 10 U/L, Average < 20 U/L
Male < 60 U/L, Female < 40 U/L, Average < 55 U/L
items.exp: Normal ALT values are: male < 23 U/L, female < 19 U/L, with an average upper limit < 30 U/L. (Book p988)

items.q: Fill up: In healthy individuals, the serum concentration of ALT is higher than AST (ALT > AST) because AST is cleared rapidly from circulation by the ______.
items.exp: Normally ALT > AST because AST is cleared rapidly from the circulation by the reticuloendothelial system. (Book p988)

items.q: Match each transaminase with its intracellular location and tissue specificity — 1) ALT (SGPT) 2) AST (SGOT) … A) Cytoplasmic and mitochondrial location; present in liver, cardiac muscle, and skeletal muscle B) Purely cytoplasmic location; liver-specific
items.exp: ALT is purely cytoplasmic and liver-specific; AST is both cytoplasmic and mitochondrial and found in liver, heart, and skeletal muscle. (Book p988)

items.q: Which co-factor is required by both Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT) and Aspartate Aminotransferase (AST)?
items.exp: Both transaminases require Pyridoxal phosphate (PLP / Vitamin B6) as an essential co-factor. (Book p988)

items.q: A 26-year-old man presents with malaise, fever, and anorexia for 3 days. Today he notices yellowing of his eyes and dark urine. Laboratory testing demonstrates marked transaminitis with ALT significantly higher than AST. What is the diagnosis?
opts: Acute viral hepatitis in the icteric phase following prodrome
Chronic alcoholic liver disease with active consumption
items.exp: Acute hepatitis presents with a 2–3 day prodrome followed by mixed jaundice and transaminitis where ALT > AST. (Book p988)

items.q: Assess the two statements on transaminases: I AST is a specific marker for hepatocellular injury and is not elevated in muscle disease. II ALT is purely cytoplasmic, whereas AST has both cytoplasmic and mitochondrial fractions.
items.exp: Statement I is false because AST is also elevated in rhabdomyolysis and myocardial ischemia. Statement II is true because ALT is cytoplasmic while AST is cytoplasmic and mitochondrial. (Book p988)

items.q: Fill up: In acute hepatitis, hepatocellular inflammation typically produces a prodromal phase of 2–3 days, after which the patient develops transaminitis accompanied by ______ jaundice.
items.exp: The flowchart notes that after a prodromal phase of 2–3 days, acute hepatitis leads to mixed jaundice plus transaminitis. (Book p988)
